source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure routing distribution, expert capacity overflow, all-to-all time, token dropping/padding, placement, batch composition, and compare routing/capacity policies.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions: routing is top-k or an equivalent sparse router; expert capacity, placement, batching, and routing policy are configurable; and clocks or trace timestamps can be synchronized. Treat uneven load and tail latency as observations, not proof that routing skew is causal.

Likely mechanisms include concentrated router assignments or high top-k entropy, insufficient capacity causing overflow/dropped or padded tokens, queueing and expert compute imbalance, cross-device all-to-all contention, poor expert-to-GPU/NIC/NUMA placement, batch-composition effects, admission bursts, and software or thermal interference. A falsifiable hypothesis is that hot-expert concentration and/or cross-device communication causes the tail: reducing routing skew or improving locality/capacity will reduce p95/p99 end-to-end latency and queue time without exceeding a predeclared token-loss or quality budget.

Instrument per request, batch, expert, and device: routed-token counts and fractions, top-k probabilities/entropy, max/mean load and coefficient of variation, capacity factor, overflow/dropped-token and padding counts, queue/service/expert-compute time, dispatch/combine and all-to-all bytes/duration, retries/errors, placement/locality, batch size and sequence lengths, throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU/NIC/memory utilization, and output correctness or quality. Report units, synchronized timestamps, and uncertainty.

Run fixed-seed or reproducible replay with the same model, hardware/topology, software, request mix, sequence lengths, concurrency, warm-up, and admission policy. Randomize matched trials or use a factorial design that changes one factor at a time or orthogonally: routing policy, capacity factor, expert placement, and batching. Include single-device/locality and no-skew or synthetic-balanced controls, plus topology and kernel controls. Compare quality and exact-output/reference checks so lower latency cannot be purchased by silent token loss.

Confounders include workload mix, sequence-length variance, warm-up, caching, kernel versions, clock throttling, host scheduling, NIC oversubscription, network congestion, concurrent tenants, admission/backpressure, and measurement-clock error. First localize whether queueing, expert compute, or communication dominates; do not claim a routing fix from aggregate latency alone.

Roll out read-only tracing or shadow evaluation first, then a small bounded canary with rate and capacity limits. Define rollback gates before testing: revert if p99/SLO, correctness/quality, overflow/drop rate, error rate, memory, or fairness worsens beyond agreed bounds; retain the baseline policy and safe admission/backpressure fallback. Evidence_required: synchronized per-stage traces, repeated matched trials with confidence intervals, topology/placement metadata, and correctness plus token-accounting checks. Results are provisional until these measurements are obtained.

Instrument per request, batch, expert, and device: routed-token counts and fractions, top-k probabilities/entropy, max/mean load and coefficient of variation, capacity factor, overflow/dropped-token and padding counts, queue/service/expert-compute time, dispatch/combine and all-to-all bytes/duration, retries/errors, placement/locality, batch size and sequence lengths, throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU/NIC/memory utilization, and output correctness or quality. Report units, synchronized timestamps, and uncertainty.

Run fixed-seed or reproducible replay with the same model, hardware/topology, software, request mix, sequence lengths, concurrency, warm-up, and admission policy. Randomize matched trials or use a factorial design that changes one factor at a time or orthogonally: routing policy, capacity factor, expert placement, and batching. Include single-device/locality and no-skew or synthetic-balanced controls, plus topology and kernel controls. Compare quality and exact-output/reference checks so lower latency cannot be purchased by silent token loss.

Confounders include workload mix, sequence-length variance, warm-up, caching, kernel versions, clock throttling, host scheduling, NIC oversubscription, network congestion, concurrent tenants, admission/backpressure, and measurement-clock error. First localize whether queueing, expert compute, or communication dominates; do not claim a routing fix from aggregate latency alone.

Roll out read-only tracing or shadow evaluation first, then a small bounded canary with rate and capacity limits. Define rollback gates before testing: revert if p99/SLO, correctness/quality, overflow/drop rate, error rate, memory, or fairness worsens beyond agreed bounds; retain the baseline policy and safe admission/backpressure fallback. Evidence_required: synchronized per-stage traces, repeated matched trials with confidence intervals, topology/placement metadata, and correctness plus token-accounting checks. Results are provisional until these measurements are obtained.
